question: In 1654 the Chevalier de Méré bet on rolling at least one six in four throws of a die. What was his chance, in percent?
answer: 51.8%, a small edge. His other bet, a double six in 24 throws of two dice, came to 49.1% and lost; Pascal and Fermat's letters on such puzzles began probability theory.
move: For at least once, find the chance of never, then subtract it from one.
ask: Which at-least-once risk have I judged by adding chances together?
trap: 67%, adding four chances of one in six.
hint: Work out the chance of no six at all, then subtract it from 1.
